key_insight: Input-convex neural surrogates make interaction-aware lane-change trajectory planning tractable through linear programming embeddings that are exact at optimality.
engineering_relevance: The framework reduces the computational burden of incorporating learned safety and comfort costs into automated-vehicle planning in mixed traffic.
method: Represent lane-change trajectories with Bézier curves.
Combine input-convex recurrent, fully convex, and partially convex networks to estimate safety costs; use another fully convex network for lateral comfort.
Embed the surrogates with linear programming formulations, avoiding binary variables required by conventional mixed-integer embeddings.
evidence_signal: On hybrid real-world and simulated trajectories, surrogate accuracy was competitive with unconstrained baselines and optimization was faster than conventional MIPs; closed-loop simulations reduced weighted planning cost.
watch_item: Exact surrogate embeddings do not guarantee real-world safety, and the abstract provides no on-road validation or quantitative runtime results.
paper_title: Optimization-based lane-changing trajectory planning in mixed traffic with embedded input convex neural networks
